headline: US stocks trade mixed near records as Hormuz peace hopes and firm crude prices drive sector rotation amid AI infrastructure deals ahead of key inflation data
raw_text:
- Major US indices trade mixed but hover near record levels, with the Russell 2000 (IWM) outperforming as small caps benefit from a risk-on tone.
- Hopes for a US–Iran Hormuz peace arrangement lift sentiment, raising expectations of eased oil-supply tensions and lower energy-driven inflation ahead of tomorrow’s inflation readings.
- Energy leads as crude (@CL) firms around $82 after briefly testing higher, supported by ongoing geopolitical tensions and US strategic petroleum reserves at their lowest since 1983.
- Industrials and healthcare outperform, while technology sees mixed flows after an earlier modest drag.
- Nvidia (NVDA) advances on news of a $500 billion AI infrastructure partnership with major Wall Street firms, reinforcing broader AI and infrastructure themes.
- Riot Platforms (RIOT) gains sharply after striking a $9.1 billion data center deal with Anthropic, tying into AI data-center demand.
- Cardinal Health (CAH) rises following a fiscal Q4 earnings beat and issuance of strong 2027 EPS guidance.
- On Holding (ONON) sinks after missing Q2 sales expectations, while LIF (LIF) slides on its earnings and guidance update.
- Intel (INTC) trades lower after announcing an upsized $20 billion share sale priced at about a 6.5% discount.
- Other notable movers include NIQ (NIQ), FRMI (FRMI), ALMR (ALMR), and RNW (RNW) with double-digit gains, while Lumentum (LITE) trades quietly ahead of earnings despite signs of an emerging optical recovery.
